entries.title: Not in an EAI project.
why: The current folder does not contain the project markers created by eai init.
The command needs a project root so it can read local app configuration safely.
You may be one directory above or below the generated app folder.
evidenceToCheck: Current working directory.
Whether package.json and src/eai.config/object-types.ts exist.
Whether eai verify reports the same project-root issue.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the current folder before changing anything.
Check whether the current folder is an EAI project.
If this is an EAI project, inspect template drift without writing files.

fixes.purpose: Move into a folder that has already been initialized.
Create a new EAI app project when this folder should become one.

stopWhen: The folder still has no EAI project markers after eai init or changing directory.

neededWhen: A freshly generated project still cannot be detected as an EAI project.

entries.title: Not logged in.
why: The CLI does not have a usable local sign-in token.
The token may have expired or been created for a different local profile.
The command needs a user session before it can resolve workspace access.
evidenceToCheck: eai whoami status.
Active profile, if a local profile is selected.
Whether the command is running on a machine or Codespace that has completed browser sign-in.

diagnostics.purpose: Show the current login and active workspace status.
Confirm workspace memberships after login succeeds.

fixes.purpose: Authenticate with the EAI identity flow.
Use a fixed local callback port for Codespaces or locked-down environments.
fixes.when: Use when the browser callback cannot reach the CLI.

stopWhen: The browser sign-in flow repeatedly fails with the same identity error.

neededWhen: Login succeeds but no expected workspace membership is visible.

entries.title: Access token expired.
why: The saved user session is older than the identity provider allows.
The CLI cannot refresh the session silently in this environment.
The command needs a fresh user token before it can call workspace-scoped APIs.
evidenceToCheck: eai whoami token status.
Whether the active profile changed since the last login.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the expired session and active profile.

fixes.purpose: Refresh the local user session.

stopWhen: A fresh login still returns an expired-token result.

neededWhen: A newly completed login immediately reports an expired token.
include: token expiry time without token values

entries.title: Permission denied.
why: The signed-in user can authenticate, but does not have the role required for this action.
The active workspace may not be the workspace where the user has the needed role.
The app or resource may require workspace admin or builder access.
evidenceToCheck: Active workspace in eai whoami.
Roles returned by eai workspace list --all --format json.
The exact command and request ID, if the server returned one.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the signed-in user and active workspace.
List visible workspace memberships and roles.

fixes.purpose: Switch to a workspace where the user has the required role.
Add or refresh a user membership and assign a workspace role when you already have workspace admin access.
fixes.when: Use for normal "add this person as a workspace member/admin" requests.

fixes.purpose: List assignable workspace roles before choosing a role for an invite.
Repair workspace admin access for an immediate child workspace.
fixes.when: Only when the target workspace is an immediate child of the supplied parent and does not already have usable workspace admin access.

stopWhen: The user lacks the required workspace role. Retrying will not change authorization.

neededWhen: No visible workspace membership has the role required by the command.

entries.title: The supplied workspace is not an immediate child of the supplied parent.
why: The child-workspace bootstrap command is intentionally narrow.
It only works when the parent ID is the direct parent of the child workspace.
This error often appears when an agent uses bootstrap-admin for normal user addition instead of the workspace member invite flow.
evidenceToCheck: Whether the task is normal user addition or first-admin child workspace repair.
The active workspace shown by eai whoami.
The target workspace shown by eai workspace info <workspace-id>.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the signed-in user and active workspace.
Inspect the target workspace before retrying a workspace relationship command.
List assignable roles when the intended task is adding or updating a user.

fixes.purpose: Add or update a user as a workspace admin.
fixes.when: Use when the goal is to add a person to a workspace or app context.

fixes.purpose: Retry the child bootstrap repair with the direct parent and immediate child IDs.
fixes.when: Use only for first-admin child workspace repair, not normal member management.

stopWhen: The supplied parent and child are not a direct parent-child pair.

neededWhen: The direct parent workspace is not visible to the signed-in user.

entries.title: workspace member invite failed, but an existing member role repair may be available.
why: The invite/add flow reached an external identity or notification dependency that returned a server-side failure.
The target person may already exist as a direct workspace member with a lower role, so retrying the same invite can fail without changing access.
When a member record already exists, the supported recovery is to update that member through EAI CLI instead of editing data stores or cloud portals directly.
Applications may cache workspace role claims in their Auth.js session or JWT, so the user may need to sign out and sign back in after a role change.
evidenceToCheck: HTTP status, server code, and request ID from the failed invite/add command.
Active workspace and profile from eai whoami.
Assignable roles from eai user roles --workspace <workspace-id> --format json.
Existing member record from eai user list --workspace <workspace-id> --search <email> --format json.
Read-back role after any eai user role set command.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the signed-in user, active workspace, and profile before changing membership.
Confirm the target role is assignable in this workspace.
Check whether the person already exists as a direct workspace member and capture the member ID.

fixes.command: eai user role set --workspace <workspace-id> --member-id <member-id> --role tenant-admin --format json
fixes.purpose: Update the direct workspace member role through the approved EAI endpoint.
fixes.when: Use only after eai user list confirms the existing member ID and the user approves the role change.

fixes.purpose: Retry the normal invite/add flow when no existing direct member is found and the failure was transient.
fixes.when: Use only within the retry limit and after read-only diagnostics confirm the workspace and role.

stopWhen: The same external service error repeats after bounded retry.
The existing member is found but role update is not approved by the user.
The signed-in user is not allowed to change workspace membership.

neededWhen: No existing direct member is found and the invite/add flow keeps returning a 5xx or EXTERNAL_SERVICE_ERROR.

entries.title: App-token platform user lookup is missing workspace context.
why: The platform call authenticated, but the request did not carry the workspace context required for app-token user or membership operations.
This is commonly seen as MISSING_TENANT or "Tenant context required for app tokens" on platform user lookup or membership prerequisite calls.
Do not treat this as the first signal to edit workspace members, role definitions, Entra configuration, databases, or cloud portals.
For platform automation app-token flows outside workspace app runtime, use the workspace-scoped platform routes instead of root user lookup routes.
If the same route works in current main but fails in an environment, the deployed PublicAPI/AdminAPI may be behind the release that adds workspace-scoped routing hardening.
evidenceToCheck: The failed path and whether it is a root platform user route such as /v4/platform/users/by-email or /v4/platform/users/{oid}/memberships.
Whether the caller is using an app token rather than an end-user identity route.
Active workspace from eai whoami and eai workspace list --format json.
PublicAPI/AdminAPI deployed versions when the failure happens in a shared environment.
Whether a workspace-scoped path succeeds for the same operation.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm login, active workspace, profile, and PublicAPI context.
Confirm the target workspace is visible before retrying workspace-scoped calls.
Verify user lookup through the workspace-scoped platform route.
Verify membership lookup through the workspace-scoped platform route.

fixes.purpose: Select the workspace that should provide app-token context.
Replace root platform user lookup with the workspace-scoped V4 route in platform automation app-token flows.
Replace root platform membership lookup with the workspace-scoped V4 route in platform automation app-token flows.
Keep workspace member and role-definition reads on the workspace-scoped V4 surface.

stopWhen: The workspace-scoped route returns the same MISSING_TENANT result.
The environment is running older PublicAPI/AdminAPI versions than the release with workspace-scoped platform routing hardening.

neededWhen: workspace-scoped routes still return MISSING_TENANT after confirming the workspace and current deployed versions.
Production or another shared environment is behind the release that contains workspace-scoped platform routing hardening.

entries.title: The application making this request is not authorized for the workspace.
why: The authorization decision applies to the client ID in the current CLI token.
It does not evaluate a different workspace app client, even when provision-me was run while diagnosing that app.
If the current user already has direct membership, provisioning is unnecessary.
evidenceToCheck: callingApplication.clientId in the structured error.
eai whoami active workspace and direct membership.
The intended app client from eai app auth status when diagnosing another app.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the current CLI identity, active workspace, and calling client context.
Inspect a different app client without changing workspace authorization.

fixes.command: Ask platform support to authorize the reported calling CLI client only if provision-me is required
fixes.purpose: Repair the caller-specific authorization without changing the target app or creating credentials.

stopWhen: Authorization state has not changed.

neededWhen: Direct membership is absent and the reported calling CLI client must perform user provisioning.

entries.title: Workspace data access authorization is incomplete.
why: The app registration exists, but the selected workspace has not completed app authorization.
The active workspace may not be the workspace this app was provisioned for.
The authorization retry may need to run again after sign-in wiring is refreshed.
evidenceToCheck: eai whoami active workspace.
eai provision entra --force --debug workspace authorization summary.
Request ID and platform status if debug output includes one.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm login, active workspace, profile, and public API context.
Confirm the intended workspace is visible to the user.

fixes.purpose: Select the workspace that should own the app.
Refresh sign-in wiring and retry app authorization for the active workspace.
Create or refresh the current user membership after app authorization succeeds.
fixes.when: Run only after provision entra no longer reports incomplete workspace authorization.

stopWhen: The same platform 5xx or authorization status remains after bounded retry.

neededWhen: The platform authorization step continues to fail after bounded retry.

entries.title: workspace app authorization could not be completed because the platform returned a server error.
why: The CLI tried to authorize the app for the selected workspace, but the platform returned a server-side failure.
This is usually not fixed by changing local files or repeatedly rotating app credentials.
The safest next step is a bounded retry followed by escalation with the request evidence.
evidenceToCheck: HTTP status from eai provision entra --force --debug.
Request ID if present.
Whether the same status repeats after bounded retry.

diagnostics.purpose: Retry once with product-safe diagnostics and request identifiers.
Confirm the active workspace and profile are still correct.

stopWhen: The same 5xx status repeats after bounded retry.

neededWhen: A platform 5xx repeats for the same authorization command.

entries.title: workspace plan does not allow this builder operation.
why: The workspace is reachable, but the requested builder operation is gated by the workspace plan.
The CLI cannot self-upgrade a workspace plan.
Read-only checks may still work while write/build actions are blocked.
evidenceToCheck: Workflow readiness status and reason code.
workspace active status from eai whoami.
Which command attempted a builder write.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm whether builder operations are available for the active workspace.
Confirm the active workspace before asking an admin to change plan state.

stopWhen: The readiness reason is paid_upgrade_required. Retrying does not activate the workspace plan.

neededWhen: A builder operation is required and readiness reports paid_upgrade_required.

entries.title: Object Type validation failed.
why: At least one local Object Type definition does not match the schema rules enforced by the CLI or platform.
Common causes include invalid default values, incomplete storage metadata, or missing required fields.
Publishing cannot continue until the local definitions validate.
evidenceToCheck: Validation details printed by eai types validate.
Object Type name and property path in the error output.
Whether the Object Type is marked published before storage metadata is ready.

diagnostics.purpose: Validate local Object Types without publishing them.
Compare local definitions with published workspace state after validation passes.

fixes.purpose: Publish the corrected definitions after validation passes.
fixes.when: Run only after eai types validate is clean.

stopWhen: The same validation issue is reported. Fix the local Object Type definition before retrying.

neededWhen: The definition appears valid but the CLI still rejects it.

entries.title: The app Object Type manifest request did not match the deployed platform contract.
why: The source Object Type schema is not the app-manifest HTTP request schema.
Some deployed platform releases derive the transport slug from the validated model name. Other releases accept the explicit source slug.
The CLI stops instead of using name derivation when that would change an established stored slug.
The current CLI supports both request shapes. A repeated failure can indicate an older CLI or a separate field validation error.
evidenceToCheck: Installed CLI version and update status.
Local Object Type validation result.
The request ID returned after the CLI tried both supported request shapes.

diagnostics.purpose: Check whether the installed CLI includes app-manifest compatibility support.
Validate source names, slugs, relationships, and storage metadata without publishing.
Confirm the CLI can load the intended workspace scope without changing platform state.

fixes.purpose: Install the CLI release that negotiates the deployed app-manifest request shape.
fixes.when: Run when eai update --check reports an older CLI.

fixes.purpose: Publish once through the maintained compatibility adapter.
fixes.when: Run after update and local validation succeed.

stopWhen: The current CLI reports that both supported app-manifest request shapes failed.
The CLI reports that the deployed platform needs explicit slug support to preserve an established stored slug.

neededWhen: Both supported request shapes fail after the CLI is current and local validation succeeds.
The deployed platform cannot accept an established slug that differs from name derivation.
include: request IDs for both rejected requests

entries.title: Object Type is not published for the active workspace.
why: The resource command is asking for a type that is not available in the active workspace schema.
The local Object Types may not have been published yet.
The active workspace may not be the workspace where the Object Type was published.
evidenceToCheck: Published type list from eai resources schema.
Active workspace from eai whoami.
Local Object Type definitions from eai types validate.

diagnostics.purpose: List published Object Types visible to the active workspace.
Check local definitions before publishing.

fixes.purpose: Publish local Object Types to the active workspace.
Switch to the workspace where the Object Type was published.
fixes.when: Use when the active workspace is wrong.

stopWhen: The type is still absent from eai resources schema after publishing and schema propagation.

neededWhen: types seed reports convergence but resources schema never shows the Object Type.

entries.title: Semantic resource search is not ready for this workspace.
why: The v4 resource search endpoint can be available for full-text search while semantic search modes are still not ready.
Hybrid and vector search need an additional semantic-search capability before the platform can create query embeddings.
This is not fixed by retrying the same hybrid or vector search command; use full-text search or check readiness first.
This guidance applies to eai resources commands using the public v4 resource surface.
evidenceToCheck: Search capabilities from eai resources storage doctor.
Whether the failed command used --hybrid, --vector, or the default hybrid mode.
Published Object Types from eai resources schema.

diagnostics.purpose: Check whether fulltext, hybrid, and vector search are ready for the active workspace.
Confirm the workspace has published Object Types to search.

fixes.purpose: Run a full-text search path that does not require semantic-search readiness.
fixes.when: Use this when storage doctor reports fulltext ready but hybrid/vector unavailable.

stopWhen: The same hybrid or vector command still reports semantic-search readiness as unavailable.
Full-text search also fails, which means the issue is broader than semantic-search readiness.

neededWhen: The app requires hybrid or vector search and storage doctor keeps reporting those modes unavailable.

entries.title: The PublicAPI v4 resource mutation contract is invalid.
why: PublicAPI v4 intentionally rejects legacy flat resource bodies and PATCH updates.
Create requires POST with {"data": {...}}.
Update requires PUT with {"data": {...}, "version": n}, where n is the latest resource version.
A resource action requires POST with {"params": {...}} and returns the new version for any follow-up update.
evidenceToCheck: The HTTP method and path used by the failed request.
The server error code and expected contract in the response.
The latest resource version when an update follows another mutation or action.

diagnostics.purpose: Read the current resource and version before an update.
diagnostics.when: Required for updates, especially after an action or another writer.

fixes.purpose: Create a resource using the strict v4 data envelope.
Update a resource with PUT and the latest optimistic-lock version.
Execute a resource action with the strict params envelope.

stopWhen: The corrected method and body still return the same contract error.
The update uses the latest version but returns a version conflict.

neededWhen: A request matching the documented strict v4 method and envelope is still rejected.

entries.title: Workflow runtime binding requires operator assistance.
why: The workspace and workflow key are recognized, but an executable runtime binding is not available yet.
Some workflow bindings require an operator-assisted request before chat or workflow execution can run.
The CLI should request the binding only when readiness reports operator_required.
evidenceToCheck: workflow readiness status and reason code.
workflow status for the specific workflow key.
request ID returned by eai workflow request.

diagnostics.purpose: Check workspace, plan, and workflow readiness.
Check whether the workflow has an executable runtime binding.

fixes.purpose: Request operator-assisted runtime binding for this workspace and workflow.
fixes.when: Run only when readiness or status reports operator_required.

stopWhen: A workflow request is already queued or the status remains operator_required.

neededWhen: The workflow request is queued but does not progress.

entries.title: workspace data/schema setup is not fully provisioned.
why: The platform could not resolve an active data/schema install for this workspace.
This is a workspace setup issue, not a transient outage: the data/schema capability is reachable but has no active install registered for this workspace.
Object Type publish (eai types seed) and schema reads cannot complete until the workspace setup is completed. Retrying does not create that setup.
evidenceToCheck: The reason code in the response body.
Active workspace from eai whoami — confirm you are on the intended workspace.
Whether the same workspace also fails the data/schema check in eai verify.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the active workspace that failed to resolve a data/schema install.
Confirm whether the data/schema service can resolve an install for this workspace.

stopWhen: The response indicates no active workspace data/schema install. Retrying does not provision the workspace setup — it must be fixed by platform support.

neededWhen: A workspace cannot resolve an active data/schema install on publish or schema reads.
include: active workspace slug and id (eai whoami)
the request id from the error
the reason code from the error response

entries.title: The workspace subscription is not active, so new capabilities cannot be provisioned.
why: The platform checks the workspace subscription status before it allows a capability to be provisioned or enabled.
Only an active or trialing subscription passes that check; any other status is refused.
For child workspace creation the check applies to the parent workspace, not the new child.
The CLI cannot renew or change a subscription, so retrying the same command does not change the result.
evidenceToCheck: Active workspace in eai whoami, or the parent workspace passed with --parent.
The HTTP status and code printed with the error.
Request ID, if the server returned one.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the signed-in user and active workspace.
Confirm which workspace was the parent or target of the failed command.

fixes.command: Ask a workspace admin to restore an active subscription for the workspace
fixes.purpose: Billing is managed outside the CLI; the capability check passes again once the subscription is active.

stopWhen: The code is SUBSCRIPTION_INACTIVE. Retrying does not change the subscription status.

neededWhen: The workspace should have an active subscription but the platform still reports it as inactive.
include: parent workspace ID if creating a child

entries.title: This capability is not included in the workspace plan.
why: The subscription is active, but the workspace plan does not include the feature or add-on the command needs.
This is a plan limit, not a permissions problem: the signed-in user may already be a workspace admin.
Creating a child workspace also reports this code when the plan defines no valid child workspace limit.
The CLI cannot change a workspace plan. If the response includes an upgrade link, a workspace admin can follow it.
evidenceToCheck: The capability or command named in the error output.
Active workspace in eai whoami, or the parent workspace passed with --parent.
Whether the response included an upgrade link.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the signed-in user and active workspace.
Confirm which workspace the failed command ran against.

fixes.command: Ask a workspace admin to add the capability to the workspace plan
fixes.purpose: Plan changes are made outside the CLI; the command can run once the plan includes the capability.

stopWhen: The code is CAPABILITY_NOT_IN_PLAN. Retrying does not change the workspace plan.

neededWhen: The plan should include the capability but the platform still reports it as missing.

entries.title: The parent workspace has reached its child workspace limit.
why: The workspace plan sets how many child workspaces a parent may have, and the parent has used that allowance.
The platform checks usage before the new child workspace is created.
The child workspace create request reports this as TENANT_QUOTA_EXCEEDED; the capability check reports it as tenant_limit_reached.
Retrying does not free capacity. A workspace admin must remove an unused child workspace or change the plan.
evidenceToCheck: The parent workspace passed with --parent.
Existing child workspaces shown by eai workspace list --all --format json.
Request ID, if the server returned one.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the signed-in user and active workspace.
List workspaces under the parent to find any that are no longer needed.

fixes.command: Ask a workspace admin to remove an unused child workspace or raise the child workspace limit
fixes.purpose: The limit comes from the workspace plan and is changed outside this command.

stopWhen: The code is TENANT_QUOTA_EXCEEDED or tenant_limit_reached. Retrying does not change the limit or usage.

neededWhen: The parent workspace is below its expected limit but creation is still refused.

entries.title: The plan has no valid child workspace limit configured.
why: Creating a child workspace requires the parent plan to define a numeric child workspace limit of zero or more.
This plan has no such limit, or the stored value is not a valid number, so the platform refuses to create a child rather than allow unlimited children.
Platform-level administrator accounts see this code directly; other accounts see capability_not_in_plan for the same condition.
The CLI cannot set a plan limit, so the plan configuration must be corrected by platform support.
evidenceToCheck: The parent workspace passed with --parent.
The HTTP status and code printed with the error.
Request ID, if the server returned one.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the signed-in user and active workspace.

stopWhen: The code is TENANT_LIMIT_UNCONFIGURED. Retrying does not configure the plan limit.

neededWhen: A child workspace is refused because the parent plan has no valid child workspace limit.

entries.title: This capability is not available for the workspace.
why: The capability check found no rule that allows this capability for the workspace and operation, so it returned its default denial.
This differs from capability_not_in_plan, which names a plan gap, and tenant_admin_required, which names a missing role.
The cause cannot be told from this code alone, so confirm the active workspace and the command first.
evidenceToCheck: The capability or command named in the error output.
Active workspace in eai whoami.
Request ID, if the server returned one.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the signed-in user and active workspace.
Confirm the intended workspace is visible to the user.

fixes.purpose: Select the workspace the capability should be used in.
fixes.when: Run only when the active workspace is not the one you intended.

stopWhen: The intended workspace is selected and the code is still CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE.

neededWhen: The intended workspace is selected and the capability is still reported as unavailable.

entries.title: Child workspace capacity could not be confirmed.
why: Before creating a child workspace the platform asks the capability check whether the parent has room for another child.
That check returned no usable answer, so the platform refused the request instead of guessing.
This is not a plan limit; a plan limit is reported as TENANT_QUOTA_EXCEEDED.
The check can fail transiently, so one bounded retry is reasonable.
evidenceToCheck: HTTP status 503 and the code CHILD_CAPACITY_UNAVAILABLE.
Whether the same code repeats after a short wait.
Request ID, if the server returned one.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the active workspace and profile are still correct.

fixes.purpose: Repeat the child workspace creation once.
fixes.when: Run after the backoff in the retry policy; stop if the same code returns.

stopWhen: CHILD_CAPACITY_UNAVAILABLE repeats after bounded retry.

neededWhen: The capacity check keeps failing for the same parent workspace.

entries.title: The workspace has no active subscription for this billing action.
why: A billing action such as updating, reducing, or cancelling a subscription needs an active subscription recorded for the workspace, and none was found.
The workspace may never have subscribed, or its subscription may already have ended.
The CLI cannot create or change a subscription, so retrying the same request does not change the result.
evidenceToCheck: Active workspace in eai whoami.
The billing action that was attempted.
Request ID, if the server returned one.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the signed-in user and active workspace.

fixes.command: Ask a workspace admin to confirm the workspace subscription status
fixes.purpose: Billing is managed outside the CLI; a workspace admin can confirm whether a subscription exists.

stopWhen: The code is NO_SUBSCRIPTION. Retrying does not create a subscription.

neededWhen: The workspace should have an active subscription but the platform reports none.

entries.title: Workspace billing could not be verified, so the plan was not changed.
why: Before changing a workspace plan the platform confirms the workspace billing records with the billing provider.
That confirmation failed or returned data that did not match, so the platform stopped and left the plan unchanged.
The failure can be transient, so one or two bounded retries are reasonable.
evidenceToCheck: HTTP status 503 and the code WORKSPACE_PLAN_BILLING_UNAVAILABLE.
Whether the same code repeats after a short wait.
Request ID, if the server returned one.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the active workspace and profile are still correct.

stopWhen: WORKSPACE_PLAN_BILLING_UNAVAILABLE repeats after bounded retry.

neededWhen: The billing check keeps failing for the same workspace.

entries.title: No app ownership record was found for this app in the selected workspace.
why: App deletion first reads an ownership manifest that lists everything the app owns, and the platform found no ownership registration for this app key under the selected workspace.
The app key or the workspace may be wrong, the app may be enrolled in a different workspace, or the app and its platform-owned metadata may already have been deleted.
The request that returns this code deletes nothing.
evidenceToCheck: The app key passed to eai app delete.
The --tenant-id value and whether that workspace owns the app enrollment.
Whether the app appears in eai app list for the owning workspace.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the signed-in user and active workspace.
List the apps enrolled in the owning workspace and confirm the exact app key.

fixes.purpose: Plan and confirm the deletion from the workspace that owns the app enrollment.
fixes.when: Run only after eai app list shows the app under that workspace.

stopWhen: The app key is not listed for the owning workspace, or the app was already deleted.

neededWhen: The app is listed for the owning workspace but deletion still reports no ownership record.

entries.title: You do not have workspace admin access to the workspace targeted for app deletion.
why: eai app delete --target-tenant-id deletes an app from a runtime child workspace owned by the app enrollment workspace given by --tenant-id.
The platform requires the target to be the --tenant-id workspace itself, or a workspace where the signed-in user is a workspace admin.
You also need workspace admin access to the --tenant-id workspace. The request that returns this code deletes nothing.
evidenceToCheck: The --tenant-id and --target-tenant-id values passed to eai app delete.
Roles returned by eai workspace list --all --format json for both workspaces.
The signed-in account shown by eai whoami.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm which account the CLI is using.
Check whether the account is a workspace admin of both the owning and the target workspace.

fixes.purpose: Run the deletion with the owning workspace as --tenant-id and the runtime child as the target.
fixes.when: Use an account that is a workspace admin of both workspaces.

fixes.command: Ask a workspace admin of the target workspace to grant your account workspace admin access
fixes.purpose: A workspace admin must update the membership before the target can be deleted from.

stopWhen: The account is not a workspace admin of the target workspace. Retrying does not change authorization.

neededWhen: No workspace admin can grant access to the target workspace.

entries.title: The platform cannot prove a single, complete ownership manifest for this app.
why: App deletion proceeds only when the platform can list everything the app owns without ambiguity, so it never deletes data it cannot prove belongs to this app.
APP_OWNERSHIP_MANIFEST_INCOMPLETE: a record needed to build the manifest is missing a required identifier.
APP_OWNERSHIP_MANIFEST_CONFLICT: two records for the same install disagree about which apps and Object Types it owns.
APP_OWNERSHIP_ENROLLMENT_OWNER_AMBIGUOUS: the install that owns the app enrollment could not be narrowed to exactly one.

APP_OWNERSHIP_OBJECT_TYPE_AMBIGUOUS, APP_OWNERSHIP_OBJECT_TYPE_NOT_FOUND and APP_OWNERSHIP_OBJECT_TYPE_INVALID: an Object Type the manifest relies on has several matches, cannot be found, or is not shaped as expected.
APP_OWNERSHIP_STORAGE_ROUTE_INVALID: the app enrollment Object Type has no complete storage binding.
These are platform data problems, so changing local files or repeating eai app delete does not fix them.
evidenceToCheck: The exact code in the response body.
The app key and the owning workspace ID.
Whether eai app delete stopped at its planning step.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the signed-in user and active workspace.
Confirm the app is enrolled in the workspace you are deleting from.

stopWhen: Any of these ownership codes is returned. The ownership data must be repaired by platform support before deletion can be planned.

neededWhen: The app must be deleted but the platform cannot resolve its ownership manifest.

entries.title: The app ownership registration request is invalid.
why: When an app is created or provisioned the platform registers which Object Types the app owns. This request was rejected before any ownership was recorded.
APP_OWNERSHIP_SCOPE_INVALID_APP_KEY: the app key is not a lowercase identifier of letters, digits and hyphens that starts and ends with a letter or digit.
APP_OWNERSHIP_SCOPE_INVALID_OBJECT_TYPES: the Object Type list is not a list, or contains a slug that is not a lowercase identifier.
APP_OWNERSHIP_SCOPE_INVALID_BODY: the request is missing the Object Type list or carries other fields.
Well-formed input is normally checked before this step, so check the app key and Object Type slugs first and confirm the CLI is current.
evidenceToCheck: The app key and Object Type slugs used by the failed command.
The installed CLI version from eai --version.
The exact code in the response body.

entries.title: The platform cannot safely register ownership of this app.
why: When an app is created or provisioned the platform adds the app and its Object Types to the workspace install record. It refuses when it cannot prove the addition is safe, so it never claims data that belongs to another app.
APP_OWNERSHIP_SCOPE_INSTALL_NOT_FOUND: the workspace has no active data/schema install to register against. This is a workspace setup gap, like tenant_data_install_no_match.

APP_OWNERSHIP_SCOPE_INSTALL_INCOMPLETE, APP_OWNERSHIP_SCOPE_INSTALL_AMBIGUOUS and APP_OWNERSHIP_SCOPE_INSTALL_CONFLICT: the workspace install record is missing required identity fields, appears more than once, or disagrees with its stored copy.
APP_OWNERSHIP_SCOPE_AMBIGUOUS and APP_OWNERSHIP_SCOPE_EXISTING_SCOPE_INVALID: an install already holds more than one scope for this app key, or a scope without a valid app key.
APP_OWNERSHIP_SCOPE_OBJECT_TYPE_NOT_EXCLUSIVE: a requested Object Type is not published as a workspace-owned type, or does not match exactly one definition.
APP_OWNERSHIP_SCOPE_OBJECT_TYPE_CONFLICT: a requested Object Type is already owned by a different app in the same workspace.
Retrying does not change any of these results.
evidenceToCheck: The exact code in the response body.
The app key, the workspace ID and the Object Type slugs the app uses.
Whether eai types diff shows the app Object Types as published.

entries.title: The app ownership record changed while it was being updated.
why: The platform checks that the workspace install record is unchanged before it writes, so two changes cannot overwrite each other, and another change landed between the read and the write.
The ownership registration is idempotent, so repeating the same request once the competing change finishes is safe.
Creating or provisioning more than one app in the same workspace at the same time can cause this.
evidenceToCheck: Other CLI runs, pipelines or admins changing apps in the same workspace.
Whether the code repeats after a short wait.
Request ID, if the server returned one.

entries.title: App ownership registration failed unexpectedly.
why: The platform returned a server-side failure while registering which Object Types the app owns, and it did not identify a more specific cause.
Problems with the request itself return their own codes, so this points at the platform rather than at the app key or Object Types you supplied.
Registration only adds ownership and never removes it, so one later bounded retry is safe.
evidenceToCheck: HTTP status 500 and the code APP_OWNERSHIP_SCOPE_FAILED.
Whether the same code repeats after a short wait.
Request ID, if the server returned one.
